name: Draw Dominoes
description: One of the simplest and most common domino games: form a single line by matching ends; if you cannot play, draw from the boneyard until you can play or only two tiles remain. First to empty hand or lowest pips in a blocked game wins the hand; play to 100 (2P/partnership) or 61 (3–4P).
deck: Double-6 domino set; 7 tiles each for 2–3 players, 6 each for 4; remainder is boneyard.

history.origins: Draw Dominoes is documented in published rule references and long-running table play traditions. Modern dominoes first appeared in France in the mid-18th century and spread to Great Britain, Austria, Germany and Italy; Draw Dominoes is one of the simplest and most common Western domino games.

setup.deck: Double-6 domino set; 7 tiles each for 2–3 players, 6 for 4; remainder stays in the boneyard.
setup.dealing: 7 tiles each for 2–3 players, 6 for 4 players; remainder stays in the boneyard. Players draw for lead; turn to lead passes to the left of the previous leader after each hand.

rules.objective: Empty your hand first by matching tile ends to the line, or have the fewest pips when the game is blocked. Draw from the boneyard when you cannot play. Game is played to 100 points (2P/partnership) or 61 (3–4P).
rules.gameplay: Players take turns adding tiles to either end of a single line, matching ends. Doubles are played across the line. If you cannot play, draw from the boneyard until you play a tile or the boneyard is reduced to two tiles (the last two are never drawn); with only two left and no play, pass. Hand ends when one player dominoes or the layout is blocked. Lowest pips in hand wins the hand; winner scores sum of losers' pips minus own total; tie for lowest scores nothing.
keyRules: Match tile ends to either end of the line; doubles played across.
Draw from boneyard when unable to play until you can play or boneyard has two tiles.
Last two boneyard tiles are never drawn; if blocked with two left, pass.
Hand ends at first domino or when blocked; lowest pips wins hand; first to 100 (or 61 in 3–4P) wins game.

scoring.description: At end of hand each player counts pips in hand; lowest wins the hand and scores sum of losers' pips minus own total. Tie for lowest scores nothing. Game ends when a player reaches 100 (2P/partnership) or 61 (3–4P).
